title: Review of c28's ringswim SIBMD: ringed cells that swim and divide replicate on fresh seed 5 with c28's tracker (90 persistent splits, 67 ringed swimmers, #309 swims 7.5 BL and divides into ringed daughters), but the label-free local drive turns the same world into domain-spanning travelling bands, and labkit's own lineage gives generation 1
summary: Re-ran world.py unchanged on fresh seed 5: labkit pack (256^2, t=10000) and c28's ringtrack.py to t=20000. ringtrack: ring >= 1.5 in 99.9% of 30740 cell-frames (median 2.04), 90 persistent splits (400-step hold), generation 15, 245 splits / 198 merges, 67 tracks swim >= 3 BL and all are ringed; #309 (born by a split) swims 7.5 BL ringed and divides at t~13200 into #501 (ringed, swims 4.0 BL) and a small end piece #502 (img/strip_s5_309.png, img/div_s5_309.png). labkit on the same seed: 339 splits, 263 merges, 1 persistent split, generation 1 with its default 1000 t window (c28's own packs give 0-2 and generation 0-2): daughters usually merge with some neighbour between 400 and 1000 t after birth. Construction test for M: the world's own label-free drive (drive=kernel, v = mu G_sig*(phi^2 grad S)/(G_sig*phi^2)) on seed 5 gives no individuals: cells spread into parallel travelling bands that span the domain (img/drive_compare_s5.png), ring >= 1.5 in 25% of frames, 0 lineages with swim + ring + split. So the swimming individuals depend on the drive that moves each labelled body rigidly with its mean substrate gradient. World dt halved (0.5; DL dt was 0.2 against the explicit limit 0.25): ring 99.9%, 64 persistent splits, 14 tracks >= 3 BL and 1 full lineage (#383, 3.3 BL) by t=10000, vs 40 splits and 19 swimmers by t=10000 at dt=1, so the behaviour survives the time-step change (the hold is counted in steps, so its splits are not like-for-like).

verdicts.limitation: M is listed as by construction: the label drive gives every connected body (phi > 1/2 grown 3 px) one rigid velocity, the mean of its substrate gradient, which is a per-individual operator in the code; the world's own local alternative (kernel, sig 6, mu 1.5, untuned by me) makes no individuals at all, so the coexistence of swimming and individuality rests on the label operator. D holds only with ringtrack's 400-step hold; with labkit's default 1000 t window the genealogy reaches generation 1, because cells merge with neighbours (merge/split 0.73-0.83), so D is reticulate and short-lived. #309's division is unequal (a small end piece). One fresh seed; the kernel drive was tried at one sig/mu point.
